in-cĕlebrātus , a, um, adj.,
I.not made known, not spread abroad (post-Aug.): “ab aliis incelebrata (opp. digna cognitu),” Tac. A. 6, 7 fin. : “multa per invidiam scriptorum incelebrata sunt,” Sall. H. Fragm. 1, 57 Kritz (dub.; Dietsch reads celata).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
